title: Gatebeat: Release-train runbook and integration checklist for API/Console/Runtime
creator: Aria Patel
description:
Purpose: Create a concise, executable release-train runbook (Gatebeat) that aligns milestones, scope-lock decisions, cut criteria, release notes, and cross-team GTM tasks for the API, Console, and Runtime deliverables. This ticket captures owners, communications cadence, and the checklist teams can follow during the 2026-Q2 release window so we avoid last-minute scope shuffle and inconsistent messaging.

Scope: The runbook will cover milestone dates (feature freeze, code freeze, internal canary, public canary, GA), scope lock rules and veto conditions, explicit cut criteria for each component (API, Console, Runtime), release notes coordination templates, QA and observability checks, and the cross-functional go-to-market checklist (docs, SDK release, blog, partner comms). It includes rollback/mitigation thresholds (latency, error-rate, cost regressions) and post-release measurement instruments.

Key outcomes:
- A single-page runbook for on-call and PM leads with clear gates and owner contact points.
- A release-notes template and templated GitHub PR label workflow so notes are compiled automatically.
- A synchronized communications calendar for internal stakeholders and external channels.
- A post-release measurement and regression detection playbook tied to Console dashboards and runtime SLOs.
acceptance_criteria: Milestone calendar published and synced to team calendars
Owners assigned for each gate and contact details included
Cut criteria for API/Console/Runtime documented and approved by engineering leads
Release-notes template added to docs repo and a release-notes collector label exists in GitHub
GTM checklist items assigned and handoff plan to growth/marketing completed
Rollback thresholds and automated alerting rules defined in Console and validated via drill

2026-03-07 Sophie Kim: Design mocked up release-notes collector UI in docs repo — linking PR once label automation is merged.
2026-03-09 Priya Rao: Draft external comms calendar shared; request to stagger blog + SDK announce by one week to allow partner previews.

notes: Decision: Use 'Gatebeat' as the runbook canonical name to avoid confusion with other playbooks.

Trade-off: Holding a tighter scope lock reduces last-minute regressions but increases risk of feature de-scoping for GA; recommended compromise is a 48-hour emergency window for critical security or compliance fixes only.
Follow-up: Schedule a dry-run of the runbook with SRE and support two weeks before public canary.
